notes.title: Household — spring commitments
notes.content:
Naomi's clinic days are Tuesday and Thursday mornings and immovable. Site visits are Monday and Wednesday and mostly movable.

Everything else negotiates around those four fixed blocks, which is fewer degrees of freedom than either of us admits when agreeing to things.

notes.title: Project load — Q2
notes.content:
Three live projects. One in planning, one in construction, one in tender.

The construction one needs site presence at short notice, which is the recurring source of household scheduling failure.

notes.title: What I know and do not repeat
notes.content:
I hear about her work at the kitchen table. Committee frustrations, vendor situations, the fact that a decision is stuck.

None of it is mine, none of it was told to me professionally, and the fact that I could put together a fairly accurate picture is exactly why I do not.

notes.title: Joint calendar — how it actually works
notes.content:
Shared for commitments, separate for detail. She sees that Wednesday afternoon is a site visit; she does not see whose site or what it is about, because that is a client's.

Same in the other direction and for stronger reasons.

notes.title: Practice — where I sit
notes.content:
Mid-size studio, twenty-two people. I run three projects and support a fourth.

Mixed portfolio — one civic, one residential, one commercial. The civic one is the interesting one and the least profitable, which is how it always goes.

notes.title: Project — civic, planning stage
notes.content:
Community consultation completed. Two rounds of comments, mostly about parking, as they always are.

Planning submission in six weeks. The programme has no float and everyone has agreed to a date that assumes nothing goes wrong.

notes.title: Project — residential, on site
notes.content:
Twelve weeks in. Groundworks found made ground that was not in the survey, which cost three weeks and a variation.

Site visits Monday and Wednesday, and at short notice whenever the contractor finds something.

notes.title: Project — commercial, tender
notes.content:
Out to four contractors, returns in three weeks. Pricing is coming back high across the market.

The client will want value engineering, which means removing the things that made the scheme good.

notes.title: Practice admin
notes.content:
Timesheets, fee proposals, and the professional indemnity renewal.

The renewal questionnaire asks about every project in the last six years and takes a full day.

notes.title: Continuing professional development
notes.content:
Thirty-five hours a year. Half through practice sessions, half external.

This year's focus is retrofit and embodied carbon, which is where most of the work will be in ten years.

notes.title: Site visits — why they cannot be calls
notes.content:
You see things on site that do not appear in a photograph or a report. A junction that looks fine on a drawing and is obviously wrong at full size.

Every architect knows this and every client asks whether a call would do.

notes.title: Household — the fixed points
notes.content:
Her clinic mornings, Tuesday and Thursday, are immovable. Her committee is monthly and quorum-dependent, which means it moves for nobody.

My site visits are Monday and Wednesday and move at short notice, which makes me the flexible one by default and occasionally by resentment.

notes.title: Anniversary and leave
notes.content: Both of us book over it most years. Blocking it in advance is the only thing that works and we forget to do it in advance.

notes.title: Finances — joint and separate
notes.content:
Joint for the house and shared costs, separate for everything else.

That arrangement has worked for eleven years and neither of us wants to revisit it, which is probably the reason it works.

notes.title: What I hear and do not repeat
notes.content:
Committee frustrations, a vendor situation, a decision that is stuck.

None of it was told to me professionally. I could assemble a fairly accurate picture, which is exactly why I do not.

notes.title: Project load
notes.content: Three live. A school extension in planning, a housing scheme in construction, and a civic tender due this month.

notes.title: Site visits
notes.content: Monday and Wednesday nominally. In construction phase it becomes whenever the contractor calls, which is the recurring source of household scheduling failure.

notes.title: The tender
notes.content: Civic commission, four practices shortlisted. Two weeks of unpaid work for a one-in-four chance, which is how this industry works and everyone resents it.

notes.title: Client confidentiality
notes.content: Drawings, budgets, and anything a client has not published. Straightforward and absolute, and it is the same shape as her obligations, which is why we both understand it without discussing it.

notes.title: Household — the four fixed blocks
notes.content: Her clinic Tuesday and Thursday mornings, immovable. My site visits Monday and Wednesday, movable at cost. Everything else negotiates around those, and there are fewer degrees of freedom than either of us admits when agreeing to things.

notes.title: Joint calendar
notes.content: Shared for commitments, separate for detail. She sees Wednesday afternoon is a site visit; she does not see whose site. Same in the other direction and for stronger reasons.

notes.title: Household finances
notes.content: Joint account for shared costs, separate for the rest. Practice income is irregular and hers is not, which shapes how we handle the irregular months.
